## Measured

Every one is a NON-NUMERIC rule, so no ceiling adjustment can clear them.

| Rule | Count |

| `no-unused-vars` | 34 |
| `no-non-null-assertion` | 24 |
| `no-explicit-any` | 21 |

| `require-yield` | 2 |
| `prefer-const` | 2 |

| `no-new-array` | 1 |

Split: 150 in `src/`, 15 in `server/`. Worst single file is
`src/contract.test.ts` at 46.

## Why it is not blocking today

The pre-commit hook lints STAGED FILES ONLY. A commit that does not touch an
offending line is unaffected. The rules are on and firing -- proven RED in
b2d4252 by staging a deliberate violation and watching the hook reject it by
rule name.

The cost is deferred, not absent: the first time someone edits
`src/contract.test.ts` for an unrelated reason, they inherit 46 pre-existing
errors on their commit.

## `no-unsafe-optional-chaining` is worth reading first

71 of 165, and unlike the others it is not a style rule. It flags
`a?.b.c` and `(a?.b).c` shapes where the short-circuit does not protect the
subsequent access, so the guard reads as present while a null still throws at
runtime. Some fraction of these are latent null-dereference bugs rather than
noise. Triage before bulk-fixing.

## Suggested lanes

Per-rule, not per-file, so each is mechanically checkable and independently
reviewable:

1. `no-unused-vars` (34) -- deletions, near-zero risk.
2. `prefer-const` / `no-useless-spread` / `no-new-array` / `no-this-alias` (6)
   -- mechanical.
3. `no-useless-fallback-in-spread` (7) -- mechanical.
4. `no-non-null-assertion` (24) -- each becomes `?.` or a narrowing guard.
   Needs judgment; the assertion may be load-bearing.
5. `no-explicit-any` (21) -- narrow per module.
6. `no-unsafe-optional-chaining` (71) -- TRIAGE FIRST. Split real
   null-dereference risks from noise; the real ones are bug fixes with tests,
   not lint cleanup.
7. `require-yield` (2) -- an async generator that never yields is a design
   question, not a formatting one.

Test files carry 63 of the 165 and can move independently of production code.

## Done means

`bunx oxlint --deny-warnings src server` exits 0 with no rule disabled and no
ceiling raised, OR each remaining violation carries a per-line disable with a
stated reason.

## Not in scope

Numeric ceilings (max-lines, complexity, and the rest) -- those ratchet in
their own sessions per `_plans/750-standards-sprint-map.md`.

## Correction: the 71 `no-unsafe-optional-chaining` hits are ALL in test files

The issue body above says this rule is "not a style rule ... some fraction of

test overrides were accounted for.

All 71 are `expect(x?.y)` assertion patterns in test files. There is no
production null-dereference risk in that set.

### One thing worth deciding

Only 4 of the 10 firing rules are named explicitly in the exemplar's `rules`
block. The other 6 arrive via `"categories": {"correctness": "error"}` and
were never deliberately chosen for this repo. Worth an explicit keep-or-drop
call when the ceilings ratchet, rather than inheriting them by category.
